Chapter 7. The Role of Policy and Power.
You know, it’s easy to overlook just how much power policy really holds over our daily lives.
Rules and regulations? They can feel pretty distant—like something only politicians or experts need to worry about.
But here’s the thing: policy shapes our world in ways that are both obvious and, sometimes, completely hidden. It decides who gets access to vital resources, who’s protected, and, unfortunately, who gets left behind.
Picture a city where the bus routes are suddenly redrawn. On paper, it’s all about efficiency. But in reality, those changes make it harder for folks in certain neighborhoods—often communities of color—to get to work or to school.
The results show up fast: missed shifts, lost jobs, and opportunities that just slip away before anyone even notices.
Most of us never really see how these policies come to life. They’re made in quiet meetings, long hearings, buried in reports and memos. But behind every one of those decisions? There’s a choice—a choice about whose needs truly matter, whose voices deserve to be heard, and whose lives are valued.
For anyone paying attention, it becomes clear: being antiracist isn’t just about having good intentions. It’s about pushing for policies that actually create real equity, not just the illusion of fairness.
That means asking the tough questions—like, who really benefits? Who gets hurt? And are we willing to challenge the decisions that keep inequality in place?
At the core of all this is power.
Sure, people in government, business, or community organizations have influence. But power isn’t just something held by a few. It’s built and exercised by many—through collective action and relentless advocacy.
Change doesn’t happen overnight, and it rarely comes without a fight. But history keeps reminding us: when people organize, when they demand better policies and hold leaders accountable, real progress is possible.
The work isn’t easy, but it’s necessary. And that’s how we keep moving forward—one policy and one act of courage at a time.
